Last updated: 2026-11-05 HKT 17:10

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Wong undermined HK's prosperity and stability: CE
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said Joshua Wong was one of the “primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said Joshua Wong was one of the “primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability” after he was jailed for 10 years for conspiracy to collude with foreign countries or external elements to endanger national security.

In a statement, Lee said Wong has repeatedly broken the law over the years, adding that before the implementation of the National Security Law (NSL) Wong, Nathan Law and others persistently colluded with foreign countries and tried to get them to impose sanctions against China and the SAR.

Lee went on to say that after the NSL took effect, Wong, Law and their accomplices “showed no repentance and continued to act as agents of foreign countries and external forces, wantonly persisting in conspiring to collude with foreign countries or external forces to endanger national security, in a vain attempt to exert pressure on the Central Authorities and the HKSAR Government through external forces, betraying Hong Kong while remaining incorrigible".

Meanwhile, a government spokesman said Wong's sentence "completely shattered the illusion of individuals endangering national security that they could escape liability under the guise of so-called 'international battlefront' or 'international advocacy', and demonstrated to the international community the HKSAR's firm determination to safeguard national security".

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Top import expo opens in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on Thursday amid fanfare. It's the country's largest…
articles.fullText:
The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on Thursday amid fanfare.

It's the country's largest import expo and the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports.

Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony.

"China's continuous hosting of the China International Import Expo is not only a concrete measure to proactively expand imports, but more importantly, a practical action to advocate for an open world economy, promote a proactive, dynamic and upward trade balance, and drive global development towards becoming more balanced, coordinated and inclusive," he said.

“Everyone is concerned about trade market issues, the key is how to realise trade balance.”

This year's event, which runs through November 10, has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors from more than 160 countries, regions and international organisations.

More than 480 exhibits are making their global, Asian or China debuts at the 2026 event, the highest number ever.

This year's expo retains its six major exhibition areas and an innovation incubation section, covering areas such as intelligent industry and information technology, consumer goods, food and agricultural products, automobiles and smart mobility, medical devices and healthcare products, and trade in services. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Road worker killed in Sha Tin vehicle collision
articles.excerpt: Police said a construction worker died after being struck by a medium goods vehicle in Sha Tin on Thursday morning…
articles.fullText:
Police said a construction worker died after being struck by a medium goods vehicle in Sha Tin on Thursday morning.

The incident happened shortly before 11am on Sha Tin Road near Pok Hong Estate.

The vehicle was travelling towards Tai Po at the time.

The worker, a 61-year-old woman, was found unconscious with head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.

The 45-year-old driver of the vehicle was arrested for dangerous driving causing death.

The Labour Department said it had deployed staff to the scene upon receiving a report of the accident and is now conducting an investigation into the cause.

_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-11-05 HKT 17:23

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Joshua Wong jailed 10 years for foreign collusion
articles.excerpt: Former activist Joshua Wong was on Thursday jailed for 10 years after pleading guilty to conspiracy to collude with foreign…
articles.fullText:
Former activist Joshua Wong was on Thursday jailed for 10 years after pleading guilty to conspiracy to collude with foreign countries or external elements to endanger national security.

High Court Judge William Tam found the offence was of a “grave nature” under the National Security Law.

Judge Tam wrote that Hong Kong was in social turmoil after the anti-extradition protests, with national security and the rule of law facing high risks.

At that critical time, Wong, Nathan Law and their affiliates kept colluding with foreign officials and outlets to call for sanctions and hostile measures.

He noted the harm is “still subsisting”, as 14 officials remain on the sanctions list.

The court also took into account their persistence when considering the gravity of the offence.

Tam said overseas allies made blatant calls for such sanctions, while Wong, remaining in Hong Kong, published and bolstered those calls.

"It is clear that the defendant’s conspiracy with others ceased not because he had chosen to withdraw from it but because he was convicted on 23 November 2020 of two offences related to unlawful assembly and was remanded in custody," Tam wrote.

"In light of his defiant attitude as shown in his published messages, but for his remand, he would no doubt have persisted with the offence."

He described Wong and Law as the conspiracy’s “two ring-leaders or masterminds” and took a 13-year starting point – below former media tycoon Jimmy Lai’s 18-year starting point for sentencing, as Wong’s case was less serious.

Tam said he cut three years for the guilty plea and mitigation, leaving 10 years – the statutory minimum for a grave offence.

Two months and two days of the new term will run concurrently with the sentence Wong is already serving for a separate subversion case.
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-11-05 HKT 14:11

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: HK 'is largest cross-boundary wealth management hub'
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Thursday said Hong Kong’s wealth management sector is growing strongly and is well positioned to…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan on Thursday said Hong Kong’s wealth management sector is growing strongly and is well positioned to capture a fair share of business emanating from shifting global affluence.

In a keynote speech at the Wealth Management Summit, he pointed to a survey in July by the Securities and Futures Commission that showed assets under management jumped 20 percent to more than HK$42 trillion.

The city, Chan said, is now the largest cross-boundary wealth management centre in the world.

A survey by summit organiser Private Wealth Management Association offered a similarly encouraging picture, as it found 77 percent of member firms reported stronger demand to open accounts or book client assets in Hong Kong and that 94 percent were moderately or highly optimistic about the city's prospects over the next five years.

Chan said sentiment at this week’s Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit, which drew some 280 international leaders from the sector, including around 120 chairmen or chief executives, was "decidedly positive", with some planning to increase investment and headcount in the city.

International capital was showing fresh confidence in Hong Kong, he said, with it being reinforced by policy measures to boost private wealth management.

"Our tax concession for family-owned investment vehicles is now well established and Hong Kong is home to over 3,300 single-family offices, up 25 percent in just two years," he said at the summit.

"The New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme has received some 4,300 applications, representing an expected investment of HK$150 billion, and we have introduced legislation to further enhance the preferential tax regimes for funds, single-family offices and carry interest, which we aim to pass by the end of this year."

Chan said higher rates and uncertainty were redrawing the map for capital flows, with cash earning a return again and investors diversifying across markets and currencies.

Hong Kong is a clear beneficiary, he said, noting that deposits rose 7.7 percent to HK$20.9 trillion in the first nine months of this year.

Initial public offerings raised, Chan pointed out, a record HK$388 billion and capital is arriving from the United States and Europe, as well as the mainland, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Middle East.

He also pointed to technology and AI as a growing source of wealth: tech is now the largest source of wealth among the world's richest tycoons, and mainland billionaire fortunes rose over 20 percent to US$1.8 trillion last year.

Hong Kong is capturing it at source – 116 A- and H-share listings in the first three quarters accounted for about 70 percent of funds raised, over half of which were in AI, semiconductors and robotics, with some 500 applications in the pipeline.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK stocks gallop up as midterms fuel caution in region
articles.excerpt: Oil, chip stocks and the US dollar were under pressure in Asia on Thursday and just about everything else was…
articles.fullText:
Oil, chip stocks and the US dollar were under pressure in Asia on Thursday and just about everything else was up after US voters swept the Democrats to a series of stunning midterm election wins, a result that raised hopes for an end to the country's war on Iran.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 397 points, or 1.66 percent, at 24,316 and almost doubled its gains to be 784 points up in early trading.

The tech index rose 56 points, or 1.43 percent, to open at 3,992 while the China enterprises index too was higher by a similar margin, putting on 116 points, or 1.45 percent, to 8,174.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 39 points, or 1.1 percent, at 3,646.

That downward trend held too for the Shenzhen Component Index, putting it 118 points, or 1.1 percent, lower at 11,216 while the ChiNext Index was 51 points, or two percent, down at 2,493.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 196 points, or 0.32 percent, higher at 62,384, buoyed by declines in crude oil but with gains held in check by fears that the US midterms trashing for President Donald Trump will result in Democrats slowing the pace of AI data centre expansion.

The 225 benchmark was 104 points down at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 103 points, or 1.82 percent, lower at 5,580 on fears for AI and chip shares and was 182 points down at one stage before lunch.

Brent crude futures dived nearly 9 percent overnight, falling below US$100 a barrel.

Brent has dropped by about 20 percent so far this week.

If sustained through to Friday's close, it would make for the largest weekly drop in oil prices since a week in April 2020 when US crude briefly fell into negative territory.

Tumbling energy prices encouraged a rally in bonds, which lowered yields, pulled the dollar to a one-month low of US$1.1273 per euro, and helped stocks.

Solar supply chain stocks jumped the most, in anticipation of Democrats boosting support for renewables, while shares in data centre companies and their equipment suppliers across Asia fell on expectations of tougher regulation.

Democratic data-centre opponents who campaigned, in part, on moratoriums on the AI linchpin won stunning victories in Texas and Georgia in a sign public opinion is shifting on the booming sector.

To be sure, most analysts think it ultimately won't dent demand for artificial intelligence, data centres or computer chips but do now expect at least a temporary slowdown.

"The magnitude of the victory is what has caught markets off guard," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

At US$93.50, oil was testing overnight lows in the Asia morning as traders chose to bet that Trump, facing a Democratic Congress and hurt by high energy prices caused by the Mideast conflict, would be less likely to escalate the war with Iran.

Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the war played a role in Republicans' defeat and his vice president, JD Vance, was even more blunt on X: "The reason we lost is the war."

A resolution could push oil prices lower still, alleviating inflation pressure and reducing the likelihood of future interest rate hikes. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Israel president urges compromise after divisive polls
articles.excerpt: Israel's president on Wednesday opened talks on forming a new government with a call for compromise, saying neither side had…
articles.fullText:
Israel's president on Wednesday opened talks on forming a new government with a call for compromise, saying neither side had won divisive elections, as he also condemned "racist" rhetoric against Arab parties that made sharp gains.

More than a week after Israel's first election since the trauma of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country.

With neither bloc holding a majority in the 120-seat parliament after the October 27 vote, Herzog said both sides needed to accept that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" and to avoid new elections.

"In the current reality, in which there is no clear winner after the elections, I ask for originality and creativity, courage and goodwill, so that the State of Israel emerges the winner," Herzog said.

The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu's hard-right government.

Netanyahu has gone on the offensive against Arab-majority lists, who have the power to put Eisenkot in power if they team up.

Netanyahu has pointed to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day in what authorities called localised incidents, and accused leaders of accepting money from Qatar, an allegation also levelled against the prime minister's own aides.

Without naming any leader, Herzog, whose role is usually ceremonial, said he had "great respect" for the Arab minority, which makes up around 20 percent of Israel's population.

"I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them towards any community in Israel," Herzog said.

The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and found no evidence that would question the results' integrity.

The committee, which reflects the makeup of the outgoing parliament, approved the results with 15 members in favour and two against but 14 others abstaining.

Itamar Ben Gvir, the ultranationalist national security minister known for his provocative calls for Palestinian suffering, said his party did not accept the results and he urged the arrest of Arab-Israeli party leaders.

Several Israeli media outlets said authorities were investigating Arab lawmaker Ayman Odeh for allegedly taking foreign money. He is part of the largest Arab group, the Joint List, which in a statement denounced "political persecution".

Eisenkot, a former military chief who has vowed to turn the page on Netanyahu's long, divisive reign, accused the prime minister of trying to "undermine Israeli democracy" and inflame sentiment against elected officials.

"We will not allow the State of Israel to be dragged into a dark abyss, far beyond the bounds of democratic conduct," Eisenkot said, as he marked the 1995 assassination of prime minister Yitzhak Rabin.

Eisenkot has warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

Opposition lawmakers said Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, in which Democrats trounced Trump's Republicans, reinforced the need to remove Netanyahu.

Democrats have vowed a tougher line on Israel amid outrage over the devastation wrought by the war in Gaza. Trump said as voting was underway that he had agreed with Netanyahu to end nearly US$4 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of the year.

"The continued tenure of Netanyahu and Ben Gvir could lead Israel down a path of international sanctions, international isolation and a clash with the US, our friend and most important ally," said Yair Golan, who heads the most left-wing party within the opposition bloc.

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a "broad national government" – with himself at the top. He faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he leaves office.

Herzog's statements have raised speculation that he could sound out leaders on a possible unity government, but Eisenkot and his allies have ruled that out.

Herzog will hold an initial two days of consultations and then give a contender 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension.

It took Netanyahu, who at the time had a better showing by Likud, 58 days to form a government after the last election in November 2022.

Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022 after repeated deadlocks. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Djokovic to miss ATP Finals after early Paris exit
articles.excerpt: Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3…
articles.fullText:
Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata in the second round.

The shock defeat by the world number 83 ended the 39-year-old Serb's hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals later this month.

Speaking in the mixed zone after the loss, Djokovic told reporters his plan for the next few weeks was "just rest".

"I'm looking forward to it," the 39-year-old added.

After sailing through the first set, Djokovic soon found himself in a battle with the Australian qualifier.

Hijikata broke Djokovic in the eighth game of the second frame before serving out to force a decider.

The third set ground on until the Serb cracked serving at 3-3 to hand his unfancied opponent a chance at victory, which he duly took with a second break to seal the match in style.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, said he felt "disappointment obviously, losing a match that I felt like I was dominating for the first set".

But he heaped praise on Hijikata for the way he responded.

"He was switched on, I wasn't serving as well and he was just playing out of his mind honestly. He was not missing and keeping the ball low and just a terrific performance," Djokovic said. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Zverev loses first match as World No. 1 in Paris
articles.excerpt: Alexander Zverev made a losing start to his reign as world number one on Wednesday as the two-time Grand Slam…
articles.fullText:
Alexander Zverev made a losing start to his reign as world number one on Wednesday as the two-time Grand Slam champion went down 7-6 (7/5), 6-2 to an inspired Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.

Playing his opening match in the round of 32 in the French capital, the German accumulated errors to tamely exit the tournament against the 24-year-old Italian.

Former World No. 5 Musetti became the fifth man to defeat a player in his opening match as the world number one.

But Zverev insisted that the pressure of being the top-ranked player was not the cause of his poor performance.

"Stress, I don't know if stress. I was a bit annoyed, to be honest," he told reporters.

"The last couple of days, because, you know, achieving the World No. 1 status is something that I think every player dreams of.

"But then I feel like I'm the only World No. 1 in tennis history that has to explain why it's okay for me to be World No. 1, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today."

In the opening set, both players staved off break points in consecutive games midway through the frame, but it always looked destined to be decided by a tie-break.

The Hamburg native got ahead 5-2 in the breaker but Musetti rallied to string together a run of five consecutive points to take a one-set lead, sealing it with a huge serve out wide to Zverev's backhand.

The Italian was now brimming with confidence and after failing to convert a break opportunity in the first game of the second set, he made no mistake two games later as he capitalised on an error-strewn display from Zverev.

Musetti continued to deploy a sliced backhand to devastating effect as unforced errors mounted on the 2024 Paris Masters champion's side of the net, culminating in a second break which allowed the Italian to serve for the match.

The world number 24 did just that, sealing his progress to the last 16 to love against a dejected Zverev.

"Personally, I felt that today, I was enjoying (it), even when I was losing in the tie-break, I kept that in mind to enjoy, you know, the beauty of this sport," Musetti said on-court.

"It paid off, I'm really, really happy."

Zverev, himself, recognised that the Tuscan was a level above him on the day.

"To simplify it, he played really good and I played really bad," the 29-year-old said.

"I think this was not a very good match from me, I think it might be one of the worst in the last couple of months." (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: WHO approves clinical trials for new Ebola vaccines
articles.excerpt: The World Health Organisation on Wednesday approved clinical trials for two new Ebola vaccines, as doctors fight to control an…
articles.fullText:
The World Health Organisation on Wednesday approved clinical trials for two new Ebola vaccines, as doctors fight to control an outbreak in Africa that has killed more than 5,300 people.

"Last month, a vaccine trial began using the Ervebo vaccine, which is approved for Ebola virus, but not for Bundibugyo virus" ravaging the Democratic Republic of Congo, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters.

"Today, WHO expert groups are recommending adding two vaccine candidates to the trial," he added.

Those two – ChAdOx1 BDBV, developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna's mRNA-1469 – were developed specifically for the Bundibugyo virus, he explained.

The DRC's National Institute for Biomedical Research is leading the trial, backed by partners including WHO, said Tedros.

"Vaccines are powerful tools, but they are not substitutes for the proven measures that can save lives now: early care, contact tracing, isolation, safe and dignified burials and trusted engagement with communities," he added.

On Monday, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) said Africa's ongoing Ebola epidemic had killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

A total of 10,444 cases have been confirmed, with a fatality rate of more than 50 percent, it added. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Real stay perfect in Champions League as City hold on
articles.excerpt: Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens…
articles.fullText:
Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100 percent start.

Jose Mourinho's side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side, level with holders Paris Saint-Germain on four wins from four league phase games.

Aboubakary Koita sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes and Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappe swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde's late winner.

Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.

Meanwhile, Erling Haaland's 78th-minute strike helped Manchester City shake off a mini-slump with a 3-2 win at RB Leipzig.

After an excellent start to the season, City had lost two Premier League games in a row either side of beating Brighton on penalties in the League Cup.

The visitors twice went ahead through a Castello Lukeba own goal and an Enzo Fernandez header, only to be pegged back by goals from Ridle Baku and Antonio Nusa.

Despite having scored more against Leipzig than any other opponents in his career, Haaland had few chances but was right on the spot to turn in an Elliot Anderson cross for the winner.

"For me I think it's easy. It's around 100 minutes a game to just stay fully focused," Haaland told reporters.

"In this period it was about trying to wait for the right moment and attack it in the right way and put it in the back of the net and that's exactly what I did."

Haaland has now scored 13 times in nine matches against Leipzig, including a memorable five-goal performance in a 7-0 rout in March 2023.

Despite the victory, City were well below their usual best against a Leipzig side in a rebuilding process under new coach Martin Demichelis.

City coach Enzo Maresca, who arrived in the summer, conceded his side were still a "work in progress" but praised Haaland.

"It's important that he's on his game. We know that at any moment he can help us, he can score goals," Maresca said.

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres scored in the first half to hand Arsenal a 2-1 win at Slavia Prague.

Arsenal got back to winning ways in Europe after a 2-2 draw at Bayern last month, reaching 10 points from four Champions League games so far, while Slavia have a single point in the standings.

Liverpool's perfect record in this season's Champions League ended in a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce in Turkiye, while Como hit nine away to Lens in an incredible performance as they equalled the biggest winning margin in the competition's history (AFP).

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks resume
articles.excerpt: Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing…
articles.fullText:
Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to US President Donald Trump.

Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress.

The results could constrain Trump's ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes.

"Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement on Wednesday.

He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating.

Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages.

Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he posted on X.

"If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf said.

Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been "defeated both militarily and politically."

The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war.

Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done," Trump told Fox News.

On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession.

"They built an anti-aircraft facility... As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely," Trump told US media, but he called it a "minor attack."

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a US MQ-1 drone was "intercepted and destroyed" over Qeshm Island. There was no confirmation from the US side.

Earlier this week the president said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," he said. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."

The president's remarks come with diplomatic efforts by mediators in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.

On Tuesday Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Pezeshkian said Iran's supreme leader had granted the government new powers to negotiate on issues previously off-limits.

Qatar, a mediator in the protracted wrangling, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal.

Both sides "are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented," Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters.

China also said on Wednesday that avoiding a return to hostilities was a top priority in its diplomatic efforts with the countries.

The war, triggered in February when the US and Israel pummelled Iran in a massive wave of strikes, has been at a stalemate for months.

Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if Washington resumes the war. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Stocks surge, oil tumbles after Trump's election rout
articles.excerpt: Wall Street stocks surged on Wednesday as markets greeted the resolution of US midterm elections while oil prices tumbled on…
articles.fullText:
Wall Street stocks surged on Wednesday as markets greeted the resolution of US midterm elections while oil prices tumbled on expectations the Democratic sweep could hasten a resolution to the US-Iran war.

Democrats seized control of both houses of Congress in a victory that gives them the power to block legislation, open investigations into Trump's administration and influence government budgets, including the Pentagon.

Heading into Tuesday's vote, some investors had viewed a decisive Democratic win as representing trouble for stocks, citing the risk to the buildout of artificial intelligence data centres.

But stocks bounced on Wednesday as analysts said the election outcome resolved uncertainty and pointed to relief that Trump did not contest the results.

Oil prices were under pressure throughout the session, adding to losses after US Vice President JD Vance said in a social media post that the Republican defeat was due to the unpopularity of the Iran war, which has sent the prices of fuel and other staples soaring.

Crude prices finished the day down more than eight percent with both major contracts under US$100 a barrel.

"I think that the election might be leading the market to conclude that Trump might now be inclined to make a deal," said Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates. "Also, with the Democrats in charge of the Senate and House, they may be inclined to restrict funding for the war, and that forces Trump into ending the conflict."

The drop in oil prices added momentum to Wall Street stocks, which opened higher following positive sessions on leading European exchanges.

All three major indices finished solidly higher, with the Dow ending up three percent, or more than 1,500 points at 53,356.

Opposition to data centres fuelled campaigns in key states like Texas, Georgia and Ohio where Democrats won gubernatorial elections previously held by Republicans.

But Wednesday's gains by Microsoft, Amazon and other hyperscalers suggest markets may see an upside to constraints that deter overbuilding, said Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers.

"At some level, people are happy that the industry might be saved from its own worst instincts," said Sosnick, who noted that Nvidia and other chipmakers fell following the results.

Both of Elon Musk's publicly traded companies fell after the billionaire's huge political donations failed to stop the Democratic tide. SpaceX fell 3.8 percent and Tesla dropped 3.3 percent.

Lockheed Martin, which lost 6.9 percent, was among the defence companies that retreated, while First Solar jumped 4.6 as the election lifted the prospects for renewable energy.

Earlier, Europe's main indices finished with gains of around two percent despite official data on Wednesday showing that eurozone inflation reached a three-year high of 4.0 percent in October.

Markets across Asia also performed strongly, though Tokyo ended lower as its tech sector struggled.

The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent, to 7,689, the Dow rose 3 percent, to 53,356, while the Nasdaq rose 1.4 percent, to 25,737. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Trump tries to brush off midterms rout and Vance split
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday attempted to brush off a stunning rebuke from voters in the US midterm elections…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Wednesday attempted to brush off a stunning rebuke from voters in the US midterm elections, delivering his first public remarks since the Democrats swept Congress in a bizarre appearance at his new White House ballroom.

Republican Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate – and his own vice president JD Vance made a very public split from him over the Iran war.

Vance said the "reason we lost is the war," distancing himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run and giving one of the first signs of what could turn into a major round of Republican infighting.

The midterms result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept through the Republican heartland, leaving him as a lame duck president for the remaining two years of his term.

The Democratic flipping of Congress signals an end to Trump's stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, probe his administration and thwart his appointments.

But in his first public appearance, Trump signalled that his priorities lay elsewhere. He took journalists to the site of the US$400 million ballroom and talked about marble and Corinthian columns without even mentioning the midterms for several minutes.

Trump eventually took questions from reporters and conceded that what Vance had said about the Iran war was "largely true because it drove the gasoline up" – a key issue for voters angered by the rising cost of living.

"But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added.

Trump added that he would "get along" with Democrats, repeating the conciliatory tone he took as the results emerged on Tuesday night, but repeated his threat to veto legislation that he didn't like.

And he warned that if his foes tried to impeach him for a third time it would "destroy" the Democratic Party.

Democrats flipped seven Senate seats that had been held by Republicans, scoring historic breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine – several of which had not changed hands for decades.

Top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said on Wednesday that the Iran war "must end" and suggested his party's incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.

Hakeem Jeffries, set to become the next speaker of a Democratic controlled House, hailed an "American tsunami" and predicted Democrats could end up with as many as 255 seats in the 435-member chamber when all the votes are counted.

"We're humbled by the outcome," Jeffries said, vowing to "fight hard for every single American, wherever you may reside."

Two Senate races – in heavily Republican Mississippi and Alaska – remained too close to call on Wednesday.

In Texas, James Talarico, one of several young, charismatic politicians put up by the Democrats, won a Senate seat. Democrats also won the state governor's race, ending decades of Republican rule.

In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated long-time Republican Senator Susan Collins.

In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932.

In Iowa, Josh Turek won an open seat, beating Republican Ashley Hinson. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008.

Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including rising star Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire.

In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, who Trump derided as a "jihadist," became the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

Democrats also won Georgia's governorship, electing former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first black woman governor in US history.

Republican candidates survived in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state's first black governor and Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat.

But the night was "a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies," said George Washington University professor Todd Belt. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.excerpt: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But…
articles.fullText:
Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position.

Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail.

Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry’s DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That’s when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities , began changing course himself.

Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether.

The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium.

That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana.

The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects.

Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it.

A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere.

It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red.

This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices.

Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it.

articles.title: What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
articles.excerpt: I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And…
articles.fullText:
I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two years ago.

While the results are striking, we probably won’t be seeing some of the big climate and energy policy shifts that have come in recent years as Congress and the presidency have changed hands. Instead, we’re entering a period of divided government, with a Congress that will likely do battle with Trump’s White House over the next two years. But even if the federal government isn’t likely to pass laws that overhaul energy and climate policy, the midterm results could be a big deal for energy, especially at the state and local level.

Let’s step back for just a moment to put these results in context. Readers might remember huge laws affecting climate and energy that were passed in just the last four years. The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act included massive support for clean energy, including tax credits and government grants and loans. Then the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act essentially slashed much of the support and financial incentives in the IRA from two years before.

What those two laws had in common was a period when the government was entirely united, with the Senate, House of Representatives, and presidency all controlled by the same party—the Democrats in the first case and the Republicans in the second.

Now Democrats have captured a majority in both the Senate and the House. But Donald Trump is still in the White House. And crucially, neither chamber is anywhere close to a two-thirds Democratic majority. That’s the ratio that would be needed to override a presidential veto.

So even if Congress puts together new legislation to boost climate measures and clean energy, Trump will need to sign it—and that dramatically narrows the scope of what might happen legislatively between now and the next election.

There could be some bipartisan compromises. One interesting bit of legislation to watch immediately after the election is what happens with permitting reform. In late September, a bipartisan group of senators put forward a bill that would overhaul how new energy projects are reviewed and approved in the US. The law aims to cut red tape and speed up the permitting process.

The Senate is set to vote on that package, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, on November 9, before the new Congress takes control in January. The White House has supported the bill, and it could pass the Senate if just a handful of Democrats join the Republican majority. But now, we might see Democrats wait until next year to try to renegotiate a deal, though anything would still need to pass muster with Trump.

With Democratic control of Congress, we’ll likely see much more scrutiny of Trump and agencies controlled by his appointees. Democratic leaders have already signaled plans to go after leaders like EPA commissioner Lee Zeldin over cuts to staff and investments. Democrats will have the power to subpoena cabinet members and open investigations.

Looking beyond the national results, a major trend to watch moving forward will be local action. Democrats swept local control of Pennsylvania, and officials there have signaled plans to support renewable energy and efforts to cut greenhouse-gas emissions. Democrats also took control of the Georgia Public Service Commission for the first time in 30 years. The group regulates electric utilities, essentially controlling much of the grid’s buildout.

Among the broadest effects of these election results, though, will be for the data center industry. According to tracking from Ballotpedia, there were 41 local ballot questions related to data centers. And overwhelmingly, voters chose to restrict their development. Nearly every single one of these measures looks set to come down against data center development, as of the morning of November 4.

And AI critics fared well in their races, too. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s seat in Texas, ousting Republican incumbent Greg Abbott. During her campaign, Hinojosa called for a law to completely pause data center development; if passed, it could have major implications for both the state’s grid and the data center industry more broadly.

We might not see dramatic new climate- or energy-related federal legislation between now and the next major US election. But many voters signaled, and quite loudly, that they wanted a change. We’ll see how much will shift in the next two years, and where that leaves us.

This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

articles.title: Govt rejects remarks on sentencing
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong opposition to remarks made by the spokesperson of the US…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong opposition to remarks made by the spokesperson of the US Consulate General in Hong Kong concerning the sentencing of Wong Chi-fung in relation to the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

The US Consulate General’s spokesperson made the comments in response to media enquiries on the sentencing.

In a statement, the Hong Kong SAR Government said the relevant remarks amounted to groundless attacks and smears, and to despicable political manipulation.

It urged the spokesperson to immediately cease making unconstructive and irresponsible remarks on the Hong Kong SAR’s work to safeguard national security, and to refrain from fabricating facts to mislead the public.

The statement highlighted that, before the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL), Wong Chi-fung, Law Kwun-chung, and others, persistently colluded with foreign countries and external elements, actively lobbied the US to pass legislation relating to Hong Kong, and openly solicited foreign countries to impose sanctions against China and the Hong Kong SAR.

In the case concerned, Wong pleaded guilty to the charge and the substance of the offence, including that he conspired with absconder Law Kwun-chung and others to solicit foreign countries and external elements, including the US, to impose sanctions against, blockade, or engage in other hostile activities against the People’s Republic of China and the Hong Kong SAR, and their officials. This included urging the US to revoke the special treatment enjoyed by Hong Kong as a Special Administrative Region under US law.

The statement said it is manifest that these acts endangered national security, and that the malicious intentions behind hostile actions by the US can been seen through by all.

It added that the court determined that Wong and Law were the masterminds in the case and the advocates at the forefront of calls for foreign countries to impose sanctions and hostile measures. Moreover, after the implementation of the HKNSL, they persisted in acts endangering national security.

The Hong Kong SAR Government, highlighting that the court sentenced Wong to 10 years’ imprisonment, said the reasons for this sentence were well-reasoned and sound. It said the court had explained that it was necessary to express the community’s abhorrence at the defendant’s acts in colluding with foreign forces or external elements to endanger national security, and to serve the imperative of deterrence.

Emphasising its constitutional duty to safeguard national security, the Government said it will continue to resolutely combat and pursue anti-China and destabilising elements, and agents of external forces. It added that it will ensure that laws are observed and strictly enforced, and that offenders are brought to account, so as to prevent, suppress and punish acts and activities endangering national security.

articles.title: CE attends import expo in Shanghai
articles.excerpt: The ninth China International Import Expo is being held from today until November 10 at the National Exhibition & Convention…
articles.fullText:
The ninth China International Import Expo is being held from today until November 10 at the National Exhibition & Convention Center in Shanghai, with Chief Executive John Lee attending the expo today.

A record high of over 400 Hong Kong enterprises are participating in this year's expo.

In the morning, Mr Lee attended the opening ceremony of the expo and the Hongqiao Forum. Later, he accompanied Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang in touring the Hong Kong exhibition area of the China Pavilion.

Under the theme “Connectivity & Enterprise”, the Hong Kong exhibition area showcases Hong Kong’s commitment to capitalising on its role as a bridge linking China and the world, and its multiple top rankings in global indexes.

Mr Lee attended the “Hong Kong Parallel Session” of the Hongqiao Forum in the afternoon. The session was jointly organised by the Hong Kong SAR Government and the Ministry of Commerce.

Mr Lee and Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao both delivered remarks at the session, while Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong also attended. Under the theme “Aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, Serving the National Development, & Seizing New Opportunities for Hong Kong”, the session attracted around 400 participants.

Mr Lee remarked that this was the first large-scale briefing session held at an international forum since the Hong Kong SAR Government announced Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, which laid out the city's unique advantages of being strongly supported by its motherland and closely connected to the world under the “one country, two systems” principle.

He said Hong Kong will continue to play its role as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”, advance its development of “four centres and one hub”, and contribute its strengths towards building a great country.

After the session, Mr Lee toured the Enterprise & Business Exhibition and showed support for Hong Kong enterprises at the Hong Kong Food Pavilion and Hong Kong Services Pavilion, both set up by the Trade Development Council.

Together, the two pavilions are hosting 71 Hong Kong enterprises, with over 60% of these exhibiting for the first time this year, showcasing quality Hong Kong products and services across sectors such as food, finance, professional services, logistics and transportation, and innovation and technology (I&T).

Invest Hong Kong and the Tourism Board are also using the expo to promote Hong Kong’s advantages and its latest tourism offerings.

In the evening, Mr Lee hosted a networking dinner, where he exchanged views with political and business leaders from Hong Kong and the Mainland. He promoted Hong Kong's professional services and I&T sectors, and encouraged Mainland enterprises to make use of the city as a platform to “go global”.

articles.title: Man arrested under security law
articles.excerpt: The Police Force's National Security Department today arrested a 34-year-old local man in Mong Kok on suspicion of committing seditious…
articles.fullText:
The Police Force's National Security Department today arrested a 34-year-old local man in Mong Kok on suspicion of committing seditious acts.

The man was arrested for the offence of “importing a publication that has a seditious intention”, contravening the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance.

Following Police investigations, the man, a local company director, is suspected of importing seditious books into local bookstores with the intent to bring hatred, contempt or disaffection against the Central People’s Government and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Under the authorisation of court warrants, Police searched the arrested man's residence and company. Seditious books, digital devices used to purchase seditious books, and documents were seized. The man is being detained for further enquiries.

articles.title: Wong Chi-fung jailed for 10 years
articles.excerpt: The High Court’s Court of First Instance today sentenced Wong Chi-fung to 10 years’ imprisonment for the offence of “conspiracy…
articles.fullText:
The High Court’s Court of First Instance today sentenced Wong Chi-fung to 10 years’ imprisonment for the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

Chief Executive John Lee identified Wong Chi-fung, Law Kwun-chung and their accomplices as being among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong’s prosperity and stability.

He said they had obstructed the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government’s efforts to promote national education, set up radical organisations, incited students to engage in unlawful acts, and advocated the notions of “Hong Kong independence” and “self-determination”.

“They further fuelled the ‘black-clad violence’ and the Hong Kong version of ‘colour revolution’ in 2019, committing a multitude of egregious misdeeds,” Mr Lee said.

“Wong Chi-fung has repeatedly broken the law, including organising, taking part in, and inciting others to take part in unauthorised assemblies, unlawful assemblies, and contempt of court, demonstrating his utter disregard for the law. Before the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law, Wong Chi-fung, Law Kwun-chung and others persistently colluded with foreign countries or external elements, actively lobbied the United States to pass so-called legislation concerning Hong Kong, and openly solicited foreign countries to impose sanctions against China and the HKSAR.

“Following the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law, Wong Chi-fung, Law Kwun-chung and their accomplices showed no repentance and continued to act as agents of foreign countries and external forces, wantonly persisting in conspiring to collude with foreign countries or external forces to endanger national security, in a vain attempt to exert pressure on the central authorities and the HKSAR Government through external forces, betraying Hong Kong while remaining incorrigible. Furthermore, Wong Chi-fung participated in the 'Project 35+', conspiring to subvert state power.”

The Chief Executive said these acts constitute extremely serious offences, severely undermining national sovereignty, security, and development interests, and directly prejudicing the well-being of the general public and the stability of society.

The Government said that in the face of overwhelming facts and evidence, it was impossible for Wong Chi-fung to deny his wrongdoing; therefore, he could only plead guilty, serving as a powerful deterrent to others attempting to collude with external forces and undermine national interests.

Noting the court’s heavy sentence on Wong Chi-fung, the Government said it shattered the illusion that individuals endangering national security could escape liability under the guise of a so-called “international battlefront” or “international advocacy”, and demonstrated to the international community the HKSAR’s firm determination to safeguard national security.

The Government welcomed the strict sentence as a vital deterrent against foreign interference and said it will seize any property of Wong Chi-fung’s that is connected to the crime.

Remarking that various western countries, anti-China organisations, politicians and foreign media have launched malicious attacks and smears on Hong Kong in relation to various cases and demanded the release of certain defendants, the Government reiterated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law.

It emphasised that all cases are handled strictly on the basis of evidence and in accordance with the law, adding that exempting any individuals or organisations from the legal consequences of their illegal acts and activities would amount to granting special privileges to break the law.

The Government said Wong Chi-fung’s guilty plea reflected the sufficiency of evidence gathered by the Police Force against him, adding that the court had set out the reasons for his prosecution in detail when delivering the sentence. It said Wong Chi-fung was sentenced under fair and open judicial proceedings which demonstrate Hong Kong’s rule of law, as upheld by its courts.

Highlighting its constitutional duty to safeguard national security, the Government stated will continue to resolutely combat and pursue anti-China and destabilising elements and the agents of external forces. It said it will ensure that laws are observed and strictly enforced, and that offenders are brought to account, so as to prevent, suppress and punish acts and activities endangering national security.

articles.title: HK global education role grows
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength, global voice and strategic vision as a premier international higher education hub. The two-day forum in Hong Kong concludes today.

Addressing the audience, Ms Choi noted that the forum gathered leaders and university presidents representing more than one-third of the world's top 50 universities. "Assembling such a distinguished constellation of global academic leadership strongly reaffirms Hong Kong's standing as an international education hub and significantly enhances the city's discourse power in the global educational arena," she said.

Ms Choi emphasised that Hong Kong's institutional strength is firmly rooted in academic excellence, robust national support and open connectivity. Citing the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, she pointed out that Hong Kong continues to set regional benchmarks with five local universities securing places among Asia's top 10.

Serving as a vital bridge between East and West, Hong Kong offers a fertile ecosystem characterised by internationalisation and diversification to bring global talent together, she said. The education chief added that the forum forms part of a strategic series of signature initiatives promoting the “Study in Hong Kong” brand worldwide, alongside major events like February’s Asia-Pacific Association for International Education Conference and Exhibition.

Elaborating on the forum's theme, "Higher Education Reimagined: Innovating for the Future", Ms Choi stressed that no matter how the global landscape evolves, universities remain fundamentally tied to economic development, societal well-being and human progress. She noted that world-leading institutions must stand at the forefront to guide this transformation as Hong Kong's educational landscape evolves.

The vision is being physically realised through the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town. The Education Bureau pointed out that under the "One Town, Five Elements" framework, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is building a holistic campus ecosystem integrating higher education, advanced research, market innovation, vibrant living spaces and top-tier talent.

Positioned at the gateway to the Chinese Mainland, the University Town will foster deep industry-academia-research integration, linking academic research directly with industry capabilities to serve national development under the 15th Five-Year Plan.

articles.title: Student assessment report released
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education Bureau, the Government announced today.

The report said that the performance of Primary 3 and Secondary 3 students in the three major subjects ­– Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – remained generally steady this year, aligning closely with results from previous assessments.

The Education Bureau welcomed the findings, noting that schools broadly agree that the TSA report provides practical data and analysis regarding student performance. Combined with internal assessment results, this information enables schools to tailor their curriculum plans and instructional strategies to enhance learning effectiveness, fully reflecting the "Assessment for Learning" ethos.

Expressing its gratitude to the school sector, the bureau commended educators for continuously adopting diversified teaching strategies to cater to the varied needs of students and raise instructional effectiveness.

The HKEAA will soon distribute school-level data directly to primary and secondary schools for feedback on learning and teaching. Meanwhile, the bureau will host thematic seminars on "Promoting Assessment for Learning" next month to support schools in making effective use of assessment data to enhance outcomes.

articles.title: Judicial proceedings defended
articles.excerpt: (To watch the full media session with sign language interpretation, click here .) Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung today issued…
articles.fullText:
(To watch the full media session with sign language interpretation, click here .)

Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung today issued a condemnation of malicious attacks and smears launched by external forces in relation to the Wong Chi-fung case, stating that Wong was sentenced through fair and open judicial proceedings.

The High Court’s Court of First Instance this morning sentenced Wong to 10 years’ imprisonment for the offence of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security”.

Meeting the media this afternoon, Mr Tang said the court had ruled that the case fell within the category of "an offence of a grave nature" and warranted severe punishment.

“I note that since the sentence of Wong, external forces have launched malicious attacks and smears regarding the present case," he said. “Those launching attacks against us are exactly the same external forces that Wong Chi-fung and Law Kwun-chung attempted to collude with. They must be strongly condemned, and Hong Kong citizens must recognise and acknowledge that clearly.

“In fact, Wong pleaded guilty, and Wong was sentenced through fair and open judiciary proceedings that fully demonstrated the rule of law that the courts of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region have consistently upheld.”

The security chief iterated that it is the constitutional duty of the Hong Kong SAR Government to safeguard national security, and that the Government will continue to resolutely combat actions that endanger national security.

“We will discuss with the Department of Justice to see if there is any need for appeal of the sentence,” he added.

articles.title: CEDD saddened by site accident
articles.excerpt: The Civil Engineering & Development Department has stated that it is deeply saddened by the passing of a contractor's staff…
articles.fullText:
The Civil Engineering & Development Department has stated that it is deeply saddened by the passing of a contractor's staff member at a work site on Trunk Road T4 in Sha Tin today, and extended its deepest condolences to the deceased's family.

At about 11am this morning, a 61-year-old female worker is suspected to have been struck by a construction vehicle while working at the site on Sha Tin Road near Pok Hong Estate. She was certified dead at the scene.

Following the incident, department representatives went to the site to learn about the situation. It instructed the project team to follow up on the incident, carry out a comprehensive review of safety procedures and measures, and offer appropriate assistance to the deceased's family.

Work at the site has been suspended. The department has instructed the contractor to carry out a thorough investigation into the incident. It will also render full assistance to other investigating departments.

Separately, the Labour Department said it was saddened by the death of the worker and expressed its deepest sympathy to the deceased’s family members.

articles.title: US trade deficit contracts slightly in September
articles.excerpt: The US trade deficit contracted slightly in September, government data there showed on Wednesday, hovering close to its widest since…
articles.fullText:
The US trade deficit contracted slightly in September, government data there showed on Wednesday, hovering close to its widest since March 2025, driven by capital and consumer goods imports and strong exports.

The trade gap in the world's largest economy decreased by 0.6 percent to US$105 billion, according to data from the US Commerce Department.

This was below the US$107.7 billion projected in a consensus forecast released on Marketwatch.

US trade flows have swung significantly since US President Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, as businesses rushed to get ahead of his sweeping and fast changing tariffs on trading partners.

In September, US imports rose by 1.2 percent to US$426.6 billion, driven by computers and their accessories. Crude oil imports decreased by US$1.3 billion.

US exports climbed by 1.8 percent to US$321.5 billion, with oil, food and overall capital goods contributing to the increase.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: John Lee visits Shanghai to promote SAR businesses
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shanghai on Wednesday afternoon after visiting Beijing, where he attended the opening ceremony of…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee arrived in Shanghai on Wednesday afternoon after visiting Beijing, where he attended the opening ceremony of the 29th Beijing Hong Kong Economic Cooperation Symposium.

In a Facebook post, Lee thanked representatives from the Ministry of Commerce, Beijing's Liaison Office in the SAR, and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, as well as colleagues from the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Shanghai for meeting him at the airport.

Lee will attend the opening ceremony of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) on Thursday.

"This year's CIIE has attracted participants from 162 countries, regions, and international organisations, with a total exhibition area exceeding 440,000 square metres," the post read.

The CE will also attend the Hongqiao International Economic Forum.

"There, I will highlight how Hong Kong is leveraging its unique strengths to integrate into and serve the nation's overall development, showcasing our achievements and opportunities."

Lee said Shanghai and Hong Kong share deep historical ties, with the SAR pushing ahead plans to establish a "sister port" relationship with Shanghai within this year.

He added that a pilot project for the mutual exchange of trade data was launched last month and is expected to benefit local small and medium-sized enterprises that export goods from the mainland.

Lee is also expected to meet with Shanghai officials to deepen cooperation before returning to Hong Kong on Friday.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: US midterm results a rejection of war: Tehran
articles.excerpt: Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if America resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes…
articles.fullText:
Iran's supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if America resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to US President Donald Trump.

Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress.

The results, which Tehran says is a repudiation of the war, could constrain Trump's ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes.

"Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement on Wednesday.

He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating.

Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages.

Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms.

"Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," he posted on X.

"If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf said.

Iran's judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been "defeated both militarily and politically".

The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war.

Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.

"I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done," Trump told Fox News.

On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession.

"They built an anti-aircraft facility... As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely," Trump told US media, but he called it a "minor attack". (AFP)
